svg.aria-label: Jewelry shipping three-layer method: soft inner wrap, rigid fitted box, corrugated outer box, each answering one failure mode

g.text: The three layers that protect jewelry in transit
Each layer answers a different failure mode — skip one and the cost moves into refunds, not packaging
plain corrugated outer — no brand name on the label
dunnage all four sides
dunnage all four sides
rigid fitted box + insert
fabric pouch
(velvet · satin · muslin · cotton)
1 · The soft inner layer — pouch or anti-tarnish tissue
Answers scratching and tangling. Chains knot and earrings arrive
as singles without it. Ask suppliers: sulfur-free, acid-free stock.
2 · The rigid layer — fitted box with insert
Answers crushing. Molded or cut inserts beat loose fill for jewelry
specifically — a rattling inner box is a broken item in transit.
3 · The outer layer — corrugated, plain, one size up
Answers the sortation belt. FedEx requires corrugated packaging
for jewelry and bans padded mailers over $500 declared value.
The two inner layers are manufacturing items — pouches, fitted boxes and inserts from 200 pieces.
The corrugated outer box is a shipping-supplies purchase: buy by inner-box dimensions plus an inch of dunnage room.
ISTA Procedure 3A is the published parcel-shipping benchmark — asking the vendor whether their mailer was tested to it costs nothing.
